messages:
Maria: Quick sync — I ran the replay harness against last week's prod traces to audit sampling/anonymization and kernel-selection parity. Posting notes now.
Ajay: Nice. Did you run any ID anonymization or session-preserving masking? Also what sample rate did you use?
Maria: Yeah — anonymization steps: replace user IDs with salted hash, keep session boundaries and relative timestamps, drop identifiable metadata. Sampling: stratified by model/route/seq_len. Sampled ~0.5% of requests overall but upweighted sequences >1024 tokens to 2.5% to get enough long-context coverage.
Maria: Example anonymize/snippet we used:
```
# pseudocode
for trace in traces:
  trace.user = sha256(trace.user + salt)
  if trace.seq_len > 1024:
    keep_prob = 0.025
  else:
    keep_prob = 0.005
```
Sam: How're we handling determinism? I remember previous replays had ~0.2% output divergence vs prod.
Maria: Determinism layers: fixed RNG seeds, pinned kernel versions, and replay of arrival timestamps so batching can match. The divergences we still see are primarily KV-cache warmup timings and slight op-order differences when the replayer falls back to a different kernel.
Leo: Current replayer is using fixed batch sizes right? That won't match continuous-batching in prod — you need to simulate actual inter-arrival and let the dispatcher coalesce.
Maria: Agreed. For the next run I used recorded arrival intervals (ms) and a dispatcher that allows continuous coalescing. Config snippet:
```
{ "dispatcher": "time_based", "max_delay_ms": 8, "max_batch": 64 }
```
Ajay: What parity checks do we compute? token-level equality? log-prob delta? kernel histograms?
Maria: We compute:
- token-match rate (exact match of generated token ids)
- mean token log-prob delta (L1)
- kernel-selection distribution (perc of matmul_fp16, matmul_int8, fused_kernelX)
- latency p50/p95/p99
Result summary (subset):
- token-match: 98.7%
- mean log-prob delta: 0.042
- kernel mismatch rate: 1.3% (mostly fp16->int8 heuristic change)
- p95 latency regression: +8% for model-x when using new kernel selector
Kate: Oof — perf regression on p95. Did the profiler show any hotspot?
Maria: Profile snapshot points to increased memcpy/quantize cost on older kernels. Looks like the new selector picks int8 matmul for mid-length sequences which increases dequantize overhead in our path. Uploading flamegraph: https://s3.redwood/replays/1764803210/prof.html
InfraBot: replayer-run-1764803210 completed. Artifacts: s3://redwood-replay/anon/1764803210/ (logs, profiles, kernel_hist.csv)
Ajay: Next steps I propose:
- add KV-cache warmup: replay first N tokens of each session to ensure warmed caches
- make sampling deterministic by seeding sampler per trace-id
- emulate continuous batching by consuming recorded inter-arrival times
- run an apples-to-apples with synthetic load (same arrival distribution) to compare
Sam: I'll take kernel-mismatch triage and correlate with quantization map. Maria, can you drop the anonymized trace segment ids here?
Maria: Dropping now — uploading anonymized segments to s3://redwood-replay/anon/1764803210/segments/ :hourglass_flowing_sand: ETA ~30m
Leo: Also can we emit a metric 'avg_requests_coalesced' so we can compare how often prod batches multiple requests vs replayer?
Maria: Good idea — added dashboard tile: replay/kernel-batching.coalesced_count. I'll kick off another run with KV warmup + continuous batching tomorrow morning.
Kate: Thanks, all. Keep notes in the replay run ticket: https://linear.app/rwd/issue/RWD-3212
